messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Auth service returned a sudden spike of 401/403 responses across multiple regions starting ~2245109800. Severity: high. Paging oncall-sre. Links: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/alerts/2245109876 :rotating_light:

maria.g: Seeing same in datadog - auth-service /v1/token exchange 401 rate jumped to ~12% for 12m. Traces show many requests with X-Forwarded-For in a tight CIDR (54.23.0.0/16).

ajay: Is this from a single client id or multiple?

maria.g: Preliminary - looks like a handful of client_ids but same user-agent and same IP block. Could be token replay or a misconfigured integration spamming bad tokens.

oncall-sre: I'm on it. Can someone paste sample logs? Avoid posting raw tokens. Redact with <REDACTED>.

maria.g: Pasted sanitized sample:
```
{"ts":2245109798,"req_id":"r-01","path":"/v1/exchange","client_id":"client-abc","status":401,"err":"invalid_grant","token_hint":"<REDACTED>","src_ip":"54.23.12.34","ua":"okhttp/4.9.3"}
```

sam_t: I see a spike of failed introspect calls from our staging connector host that was recently promoted. Checking deploy history...

elaine: @sam_t staging connector was promoted to prod last night for a hotfix. We rolled back the config change earlier today but maybe some creds were left in logs.

secops: Can we confirm whether any long-lived client secrets were printed in logs? If so, treat as exposed and rotate.

ajay: grep across logstore shows 6 occurrences of "client_secret" in plaintext in staging->prod logs between 2245090000 and 2245105000. I'll open a restricted ticket.

ops-lead: Immediate mitigation steps: 1) block the CIDR on the auth-layer WAF 2) revoke current client secrets for affected client_ids 3) invalidate sessions issued in last 6 hours for those clients 4) rotate secrets and issue new ones via secure channel.

oncall-sre: Executing step 1 now: `curl -X POST https://waf.internal/blocks -d '{"cidr":"54.23.0.0/16","reason":"auth-replay-suspected"}'` -> 200 OK. Blocks applied to edge. :white_check_mark:

maria.g: Edge block reduced bad traffic by ~90% in the next minute, auth error rate down to 1.3%. Good immediate effect.

sam_t: Starting secret rotation for client-abc and client-def. Running the rotation script in secure-runner. Command: `./rotate-client-secret --client client-abc --env prod --no-notify` (will update service bindings).

secops: Hold on the automated notify flag — we need to coordinate customer notifications. Also capture a signed artifact of rotation for audit.

elaine: Notifying product security and CSM. Drafting an internal heads-up: "Potential exposure of client secrets in logs during deploy. We're rotating affected secrets and blocking suspicious IP ranges. Investigating customer impact."

ajay: Quick investigation: the lines with secrets were from a debug logging flag enabled in a staging deploy promoted by mistake. That release included `logger.debug('client_secret=' + secret)` in connector initialization. Oof.

ops-lead: That's root cause. Add immediate action item: disable debug logging at startup and add a pre-promote check for secrets in logs.

oncall-sre: Rotation script completed for client-abc & client-def. New secrets minted and pushed to vault. Confirmed services pulled new secrets. Paste audit hash: `sha256:3f8a9c...` in secure ticket.

secops: Creating incident-ticket SEC-2026-312. Will mark as "possible secret exposure". Need scope: list all client_ids appearing in logs.

maria.g: Found additional client_ids: client-xyz, client-123 in older logs (2024-09-02 window). Flagged them in the ticket.

sam_t: Running session invalidation: `POST /admin/sessions/invalidate` payload includes `client_ids: ["client-abc","client-def"]` and `since: "2024-03-14T04:30:00Z"`. Endpoint returned 202 accepted.

ajay: Will run targeted replay detection: correlate token hashes in access logs with known leaked token pattern (hash-only) to see if any succeeded requests after leak.

secops: If we confirm any issued tokens were used, we will trigger customer-facing notification and P1 breach protocol. For now, status = under investigation, containment in place.

ops-lead: Action items and owners:
- sam_t: confirm all rotated secrets and push audit artifacts (done)
- ajay: full log grep for plaintext secrets across last 30 days -> deliver by +2h
- maria.g: metric/dashboard update for auth error rates and customer impact list -> +30m
- elaine: prepare draft customer notification and legal review -> +1h
- secops: open SEC ticket, start timeline and severity assessment -> immediate

oncall-sre: Handoff at 04:30 UTC to second shift. I'll leave a runbook note in the secure ticket with current mitigations and links. Next oncall: @oncall-sre (second-shift) please confirm acceptance.

oncall-sre (second-shift): Ack, taking over at 04:30 UTC. I'll continue correlation and escalation if we find confirmed misuse.

maria.g: Quick customer-impact estimate: at most 12 affected integrations based on client_ids; of those 4 are active customers in last 7 days. We'll prioritize contact.

secops: Elevating to P1 if any confirmed token misuse that results in data access. Keep logs and evidence preserved.

ajay: Found two suspicious successful calls that used an old token hash for client-xyz at 2245104305 to the embeddings endpoint. Investigating whether payload data was returned.

ops-lead: If confirmed, prepare legal/CS notification templates. Elaine, loop in legal now.

elaine: Looping legal and CSM. Draft will include timeline, actions taken, and recommended customer steps (rotate secrets, revoke sessions).

secops: Forensics: snapshot auth VM logs, export sanitized traces, and fork a read-only copy of the log bucket to secure-case folder. Starting now.

maria.g: Auth error rate back to baseline after blocks and rotations. Still watching for anomalous latencies.

oncall-sre: Leaving a short summary for night shift in the secure ticket: containment applied (WAF block, secret rotation, session invalidation). Investigation ongoing for token reuse.

ops-lead: Thanks team. We'll reconvene for an incident review once secops posts the initial findings. If anyone finds confirmed data exfil or PII access, mark SEC-2026-312 as breach and escalate to execs. :exclamation:

incident-bot: Incident thread SEC-2026-312 created: https://tracker.internal/SEC-2026-312. Pager cleared at 2245114520 (status: investigating).
